newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser Busch to boost stake in Corona brewer.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser Busch to boost stake in Corona brewer.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc. said Wednesday the brewing giant will pay about $550 million to increase its stake in Mexico's No. 1 brewer, Grupo Modelo S.A. de C.V., to 37 percent.
Grupo Modelo is known in the United States for its Corona brand beer.

St. Louis-based Anheuser-Busch, maker of Budweiser beer and the largest brewer in the world, continues to have the option to bring its stake in Grupo Modelo and its subsidiaries to 50 percent. It has until the end of 1997 to exercise that option.

"Today's action reflects a major additional investment, bringing the total to more than $1 billion," Jack Purnell, chairman of Anheuser-Busch International Inc., a subsidiary of Anheuser-Busch, said in a statement.

In 1993, St. Louis-based Anheuser-Busch acquired a 17.7 percent direct and indirect interest in Grupo Modelo and its subsidiary, Diblo, for $477 million, with options to increase its holdings at any time between mid-1995 and the end of 1997.
The latest investment is expected to close in late January.

For 1996, Anheuser-Busch estimates its international sales volume will represent between 6 percent and 7 percent of its worldwide sales volume. Including its share of foreign partners' sales, this figure rises to about 11 percent.
The total worldwide sales volume figure for 1996 was not available. In 1995, the worldwide volume 87.5 million barrels.
Anheuser-Busch's net sales after excise taxes for the first nine months of 1996 amounted to $8.40 billion.

Although its international business is comparatively small, Anheuser-Busch has been looking to build its international business, including investments in Tsingtao Brewery Co. Ltd in China and Companhia Antarctica Paulista of Brazil.
"The U.S. business is still what makes or breaks their earnings," Salomon Brothers analyst Jennifer Solomon said. "But the international story is, there is a lot of opportunity there."

As a result of the investment, the number of seats Anheuser-Busch holds on the Modelo board will rise to 10 from the current three. The total number of seats on the Modelo board will increase to 21 from the current 14.

"Our new 37 percent ownership level is also a milestone because it entitles Anheuser-Busch to assume significantly enhanced minority rights, including the right to approve, within specified limits, the annual operating budget, capital expenditures, multi-year contracts and the incursion of debt, among other key issues," Purnell said.
